BYOK custom endpoints: support dynamic/refreshable API key (apiKeyHelper) for OAuth-based gateways

### Feature request

The BYOK "custom endpoint" model configuration (`vendor: "customendpoint"`) only accepts a **static** credential in `apiKey` (or `requestHeaders`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`. There is no way to supply a **dynamically generated / short-lived** token.

This blocks any enterprise gateway that uses **OAuth** instead of static API keys, because OAuth access tokens are short-lived (e.g. ~1h) and must be refreshed. Today the only options are (a) manually pasting a fresh token every hour, or (b) running a local reverse-proxy that injects the token — both are poor workarounds for what should be first-class.

### Requested behavior

Add a way for the custom endpoint to obtain its credential dynamically per request, e.g.:

- An `apiKeyHelper`-style setting pointing to a local script/command whose stdout is the current token (same model as Claude Code's [`apiKeyHelper`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#credential-management)), and/or
- Support for `${env:VAR}` / secret references resolved at request time in `apiKey` / `requestHeaders`.

### Concrete use case

Authenticating against a **Databricks AI Gateway** (`/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`) with OAuth (U2M) instead of a personal access token. The Databricks CLI already mints and auto-refreshes OAuth tokens (`databricks auth token`); an `apiKeyHelper` hook would let it feed the current token to VS Code transparently.

### Prior issues

This was previously requested and closed **not planned** — #318762 (closed only for lack of 20 upvotes, not on technical grounds) and #322499 (dynamic Bearer token, incl. the Databricks AI Gateway scenario). Re-filing since demand persists.

### Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)
- Extension: GitHub Copilot Chat (BYOK / Manage Models)

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (feature request)

Show /btw chats as children of their main session in the Sessions tree

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

When a `/btw` chat is started from a main chat session, show it as a child of that main session in the Sessions tree.

Today these related chats can appear separately from the main session, which makes them easy to miss, especially while they are actively working. Nesting `/btw` chats under their originating session would preserve their relationship and make the child chat's work indicator visible alongside the main session.

The main session should remain the top-level item, with its `/btw` chats listed as children in the same way related sessions are already stacked.

Changes view is empty until opening the changed-files pill from the response

**Reported by:** @Yoyokrazy 

## Type of issue

Bug

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent/chat request that changes files.
2. Open the Changes view for the session.
3. Observe that the Changes view does not list any files.
4. Click the changed-files pill embedded in the response.

## Actual behavior

The Changes view is empty, even though the response has changed files. Clicking the changed-files pill in the response correctly opens the changed files from that response.

## Expected behavior

The Changes view should list the changed files without requiring the response's changed-files pill to be opened first.

A screen recording demonstrating the issue was provided with the [original report](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09MVCZKLP4/p1790205508222409).

Copilot agent edit: Problems panel shows errors from a superseded chat-editing snapshot, not the file's actual content

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! copilot_bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.67.0 (built-in, `copilot-chat`)
- VS Code Version: 1.139.0
- OS Version: Windows 11
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent (`github.copilot.editsAgent`)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): `openrouter/OpenRouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`
- Logs: available on request (exthost logs + `chatEditingSessions\<sessionId>\state.json` + `contents\` snapshots; see Evidence below)

## Summary

During a Copilot agent editing session, the *modified-file virtual document* (`chat-editing-text-model:/...?...documentId=modified-file-entry::N`) served a **superseded intermediate snapshot** instead of the final (`currentHash`) content. This caused:

1. **Phantom diagnostics** — the PowerShell language service computed 5 "Unexpected token ')'" errors on the mangled virtual document, shown in the Problems panel against a file that is clean on disk.
2. **Stale chat file context** — a later chat request attached the mangled text as "User's active file" (confirmed in `session-store.db-wal`).

The state persisted across VS Code restarts and was only cleared by deleting `chatEditingSessions\<sessionId>\`.

## Invariant violation

Hydration of `modified-file-entry` documents must use the **`currentHash`** content, not a superseded `originalHash` snapshot. In the incident, `state.json` recorded:

```json
{
  "resource": "file:///c%3A/Users/.../profile.ps1",
  "originalHash": "41b7364",
  "currentHash": "e07c120"
}
```

- `originalHash` (`41b7364`) = mangled intermediate (197 bytes)
- `currentHash` (`e07c120`) = clean final content (187 bytes, matches disk)

Despite `currentHash` being correct, the virtual document served the `41b7364` (mangled) content.

Extension Host debugging fails to attach on macOS when localhost resolves to ::1 first (ECONNREFUSED) Type: Bug Environment: VS Code: 1.139.0 (commit 2242ebbb54efeeb0129e08e919e7e8d43033cd83), macOS, arm64 System DNS order: localhost resolves ::1 before 127.0.0.1 (confirmed via dscacheutil -q host -a name localhost and Node's dns.lookup) Repro: Open any extension project, set a breakpoint in activate(). Press F5 (Run Extension, extensionHost launch type). Extension Host never starts; breakpoint is never hit. Observed in logs (~/Library/Application Support/Code/logs//window*/renderer.log): Root cause: The Extension Host's Node inspector listens only on 127.0.0.1, but ms-vscode.js-debug's attach logic (extension.js, pwa-extensionHost resolveParams/launchProgram) requests http://localhost:${port}. On systems where localhost resolves to ::1 first (common with certain VPN/network configs), the debugger connects to the wrong address and the attach never succeeds, so the whole Extension Host launch times out and no extension activates. Workaround: Manually patching the bundled ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js to use http://127.0.0.1:${port} instead of http://localhost:${port} for the Extension Host attach fixes it immediately. Setting NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first via launchctl setenv does not fix it — the debugger's own Node process doesn't appear to honor it for this connection. Suggested fix: Have the Extension Host attach logic prefer 127.0.0.1 explicitly (like it already does elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. the c7/Xg localhost-alias handling), rather than relying on system DNS resolution order for localhost. Agents Window: Add an extensible environment picker

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Summary

Add an explicit environment picker to the Agents Window new-session experience. Initially, the picker could offer **Local** and **Remote**, **Cloud** while being designed to accommodate additional environment types over time.

## Motivation

The place where work runs is a distinct choice from the source or workspace being used. Today these concepts can become coupled, making it harder to understand or extend session creation as more execution environments become available.

An environment picker would make this choice visible and establish a scalable model for environments such as:

- **Local** — run on the current machine.
- **Remote** — run through a supported remote connection or host.
- Future environments, such as cloud-hosted, containerized, or other provider-backed environments.

## Proposed direction

- Add an **Environment** picker to the new-session UI.
- Keep environment selection independent from:
  - Source/workspace selection.
  - Agent or harness selection.
  - Session intent.
- Start with **Local** and **Remote** where supported.
- Allow environment providers to contribute availability, display information, configuration/connection actions, and capability constraints without redesigning the picker for every new environment type.
- Remember the user's explicit selection when appropriate.
- Clearly communicate unavailable or unsupported source/environment/harness combinations rather than silently switching environments.
- Ensure the selected environment remains visible before launch and is represented consistently when restoring or inspecting a session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can explicitly choose between available Local and Remote environments when creating a session.
- [ ] Environment selection is modele

Use contextual text for the cross-posting affordance

When `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` is enabled, there's empty space above the chat input.

Feedback from standup was to avoid using an icon for the cross-posting affordance.

Instead, explore a text-based treatment. The text could be contextual and surface useful prompts such as:

- New models are available
- Relevant hints or guidance
- Other context-specific information

The goal is to make the affordance clearer and more useful than a standalone icon.

Agent Host: never auto-approve tools an admin marked ineligible

**TL;DR (admin/user):** An admin can mark tools as never auto-approved (`ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval`). In Agent Host, assisted approval and saved session approvals can still auto-approve them.

```jsonc
{ "ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval": { "fetch": false } }
```

Expected: `fetch` always asks for confirmation.

- [ ] The Agent Host permission layer never auto-approves a policy-ineligible tool: no assisted auto-approval, no session or saved approvals.
- [ ] Keep the existing Allow All lock until the runtime supports per-tool managed rules.
- [ ] Tests for normal and assisted approval, and for resume.

Agent Host: apply the network filter to web fetches

**TL;DR (admin/user):** In Local, the network filter blocks unlisted domains for the fetch and browser tools without needing the sandbox. In Agent Host, the runtime's `web_fetch` bypasses it: unlisted domains prompt, and under Allow All they are fetched silently.

```jsonc
{ "ChatAgentNetworkFilter": true, "ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains": ["github.com"] }
```

Expected (sandbox off): fetching `evil.example` fails without a prompt, as in Local.

- [ ] When the network filter is on, route Agent Host web fetches through `IAgentNetworkFilterService`, e.g. by exposing VS Code's fetch tool instead of `web_fetch`, or by checking requests in the host.
- [ ] Holds under Allow All and assisted approval.
- [ ] Tests for allowlist, denylist, and empty-lists cases.

Agent Host: forward network domain lists to the sandbox

**TL;DR (admin/user):** With the sandbox on, Agent Host allows all or no network traffic. Admin domain allow/deny lists are dropped, although the runtime can enforce them.

```jsonc
{
  "ChatAgentSandboxEnabled": "on",
  "ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands": false,
  "ChatAgentNetworkFilter": true,
  "ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains": ["github.com", "*.github.com"]
}
```

Expected: `evil.example` is blocked for shell and `web_fetch`, including under Allow All.

- [ ] Forward `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains` / `deniedNetworkDomains` into `sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowedHosts` / `blockedHosts` in `buildSandboxConfigForSdk`.
- [ ] Map "filter on, both lists empty" to `allowOutbound: false`; the runtime treats an empty `allowedHosts` as unrestricted.
- [ ] Reconcile pattern differences (runtime: a denied domain covers its subdomains; `*.x` is strict subdomains).
- [ ] Tests, including Allow All.

Agent Host: keep sessions on Local when a configured policy isn't enforced

**TL;DR (admin/user):** If an admin sets a policy Agent Host can't enforce yet, users could silently lose that control when Agent Host becomes the default. Keep those users on Local and explain why.

- [ ] When a configured policy is `notEnforced` in the Agent Host policy support list (#337536), new sessions default to Local.
- [ ] Choosing Agent Host manually shows a warning naming the policy.
- [ ] Policy Diagnostics shows each configured policy's Agent Host status.

Example: with `ChatAllowedMcpServers` set, new chat sessions stay on Local until MCP allow/deny is enforced in Agent Host.

Agent Host: track enterprise policy support per policy

**TL;DR (admin/user):** Admins can't tell which VS Code policies Agent Host enforces. Add one list in code that records each policy's Agent Host status; it becomes the burndown for Local → Agent Host parity.

- [ ] Map every policy in `build/lib/policies/policyData.jsonc` to an Agent Host status: `enforced`, `partial`, `notEnforced`, or `notApplicable`, with a tracking issue for each gap.
- [ ] CI fails when a policy is added without a status.
- [ ] Audit policies not yet checked, including `ChatHooks`, `ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly`, `ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `ChatAgentExtensionTools`, and remote Agent Hosts.

Known gaps at filing: MCP allow/deny (#328241), network allowlist (#337538, #337539), per-tool auto-approval (#337540). The list drives the Local fallback in #337537.

AgentHost: Provide an interactive way to install sandbox pre-reqs similar to local sandboxing

## Problem

Agent Host sandboxing can require platform-specific prerequisites that are not already installed. Today, users can reach a state where sandboxing cannot be enabled without manually identifying and installing those dependencies.

Local sandboxing provides an interactive prerequisite installation experience. Agent Host should offer a similar guided flow so users can install missing sandbox prerequisites without leaving the product or having to discover the required commands themselves.

## Proposed experience

- Detect missing Agent Host sandbox prerequisites.
- Explain which prerequisites are missing and why they are needed.
- Offer an explicit action to install them interactively, similar to the local sandboxing experience.
- Show installation progress and actionable errors.
- Re-check prerequisites after installation and continue enabling sandboxing when successful.
- Preserve a manual-install path for users who do not want the automated flow.

## Acceptance criteria

- Users are prompted with a clear installation action when required sandbox prerequisites are missing.
- Installation requires explicit user consent.
- The flow works for every platform supported by Agent Host sandboxing.
- Failures identify the failed prerequisite and provide recovery guidance.
- Successfully installed prerequisites are detected without requiring users to rediscover or repeat the setup flow.

Branch Changes status pill assumes the base remote is origin Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: Latest Insiders - OS Version: Linux x64 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Configure `origin` as a fork and another arbitrarily named remote as the canonical repository. 2. Create a feature branch from the canonical remote's base branch. 3. Open an Agent Session and select the **Branch Changes** status pill. **Actual:** The pill compares against `origin/`. If that ref is stale, it shows hundreds of unrelated files. **Expected:** The pill compares against the actual base ref, regardless of its remote name. The Agent Host Git service reads `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` and constructs `origin/`. There is no setting to select another base remote. Example when forked main is stale (as often time is the case): The current Branch Changes status pill was introduced by microsoft/vscode#332982, **“Chat: unify Agent Host status pills across chat surfaces.”** Related: * https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337420 uses a stale `origin/HEAD`, producing thousands of unrelated files. * https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321941 selects the wrong base branch when a feature branch starts from a non-default branch. * https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/309102 requests consistent comparison against the remote default branch.
